blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safe ACE-inhibitor to ARNI transition
stem: A provider discontinues an ACE inhibitor and plans to start sacubitril/valsartan (Entresto). Which nursing action is most important before the first Entresto dose?

options.A: Verify that at least 36 hours have elapsed since the last ACE-inhibitor dose because concomitant or closely sequential exposure increases the risk of angioedema.
options.B: Give the first Entresto dose with the final ACE-inhibitor dose so renin-angiotensin blockade remains continuous while the new heart-failure regimen is started.
options.C: Verify the client's heart rate is above 60/min and then start Entresto immediately because the transition does not require a medication washout interval.
options.D: Delay Entresto for seven days after the ACE inhibitor because a full week is the standard labeled washout interval regardless of the specific ACE inhibitor used.

rationale: Current ENTRESTO labeling contraindicates concomitant use with an ACE inhibitor and requires a 36-hour washout period when switching from an ACE inhibitor to ENTRESTO. The drug-interaction section explains that concomitant ACE-inhibitor exposure is contraindicated because of increased angioedema risk. Therefore A is correct. B creates prohibited overlap, C ignores the required washout, and D invents a longer universal interval not supported by the label.
educational_objective: When switching from an ACE inhibitor to sacubitril/valsartan, verify the required 36-hour washout interval to avoid prohibited overlap and reduce angioedema risk.
source_document_title: ENTRESTO (sacubitril and valsartan) — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: DailyMed updated July 6, 2026; current label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §2.1 General Considerations: ENTRESTO is contraindicated with concomitant ACE-inhibitor use; allow a 36-hour washout when switching from an ACE inhibitor. §4 Contraindications and §7.1 Drug Interactions: do not administer within 36 hours of switching from or to an ACE inhibitor; concomitant ACE inhibition increases angioedema risk.
source_claim_supported: A 36-hour washout is required between an ACE inhibitor and ENTRESTO; overlapping exposure is contraindicated because of increased angioedema risk.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate medication orders, identify contraindications and interactions, and safely administer medications.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four options as complete medication-transition actions of comparable length while retaining the exact 36-hour requirement.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current July 2026 ENTRESTO labeling. The exact 36-hour interval is preserved and no second defensible transition plan remains.
